rounds.proof_sketch: Kernel launched with 1D config: threads=256. blockDim.x=256, blockDim.z=1. Original store loop: stride=256 (each index written by exactly one thread). Mutated store loop: stride=1 (each thread writes ALL indices from tid to cols-1). However, all threads read identical values from shared memory (correctly computed prefix sum), so multiple threads writing to the same output[i] all write the same value shared[i]. This is a benign write-write race with identical values.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the store loop stride from blockDim.x (256) to blockDim.z (1) in a 1D kernel launch. This causes each thread to iterate through nearly all column indices instead of striding by 256. While this creates write-write races where multiple threads write to the same output locations, all threads write the identical value read from shared memory. Since the shared memory contains the correctly computed prefix sum (populated before the store loop via __syncthreads), and all threads reading shared[i] observe the same value, every write to output[row*cols+i] stores the correct result. The CUDA memory model guarantees one write persists when multiple threads write the same value to the same location, making the output deterministic and correct regardless of which thread's write wins.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation creates redundant work (multiple threads writing same values) but does not alter computed results. No value-level input can distinguish the outputs because the mathematical computation is preserved - only the work distribution among threads changes.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for GPU kernels should classify write-write races with identical values as semantically equivalent. The index_replace mutation operator (changing blockDim.x to blockDim.z) can produce equivalent mutants when the affected loop performs idempotent writes of values from shared/common memory. Consider adding static analysis to detect such benign race patterns before testing.
